challenge.better_approach: Looked at (a) exempting the tester path inside the proxy proof. That weakens the tooth, puts a tester path into inferenceproxy, and is outside the scope the orchestrator agreed; (b) building it under c620e551970f. Its bounds hold only the keeps-its-answers proof, so it can't. A one-line docstring reword in the file that carries the name is the smallest fix.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the docstring at :4 is the only hit. The proxy tooth measured exactly 1 at its 09:54 seal, and a grep of the tester proof finds only line 4. Also assumed: rewording a docstring changes no tooth's behavior. The proof's teeth build their fixtures from _HEAD/_V1 strings, not from line 4.
challenge.prior_art: The proxy proof already spells the name split (OLD = "inference" + "_domain") for this same reason. That's the idiom this follows. The red ticket c620e551970f is the tester-cast record of the symptom. No ticket rewords the tester proof.
challenge.real_collision: 6eb235ee813d owns this proof's existing teeth and stands at PROVEME. Landing this changes the proof's bytes, so 6eb2 is walked after this lands (the orchestrator's order), not before, or its seal goes stale. That's an ordering, not an exclusive collision.

answers.how: Reword the docstring at cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_rung_4_follows_a_renamed_proof.py:4 so it names the rename by its ticket (f942a413f26d) without the old name, and add one tooth to the same proof that reads the proof's own text for the retired name (spelled split, as the proxy proof spells it), keyed under this ticket in PROVES. answers.traces_to: Law 9 (red is the default; green is earned): two inferenceproxy proofs have stood red since 2026-11-18 09:51 on this one line. Law 8: the proxy's rename tooth stays whole rather than weakened by an exemption.
answers.what: The tester's rung-4 rename proof stops spelling the retired device name, so the inference proxy's 'no tracked code names the old name' tooth reads green again.

bullets.text: Measured 2026-11-18: the proxy's old-name tooth reds on 1 hit, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_rung_4_follows_a_renamed_proof.py:4, a docstring added by 6eb235ee813d at 09de7cc70 (2026-11-14). The two inferenceproxy proofs then red each other through their every-other-proof-is-green teeth.
A whole-tree name check reads comments too, so any later proof that cites a rename by its old name reds the renamed device. The split spelling is the idiom that avoids it.
